entries.summary: The game’s foundation: attributes, mastery, checks, saves, defenses, health, and damage.
entries.text: Core Rules establishes the math and vocabulary used everywhere else in DC20. Start here when you need a formula, need to determine which roll applies, or need to resolve the result of a Check, Save, Attack, or source of damage.
entries.title: Core Rules Overview

entries.keywords: Might Agility Charisma Intelligence attribute limit standard array point buy roll
entries.summary: Might, Agility, Charisma, and Intelligence describe a creature’s fundamental capabilities.
entries.text: Attributes normally range from -2 upward and are added to Checks, Saves, defenses, and other statistics when a rule calls for them. Starting characters use Standard Array, Point Buy, or the Roll Method. The Attribute Limit is +3 at level 1, +4 at level 5, +5 at level 10, +6 at level 15, and +7 at level 20.
entries.title: Attributes

entries.keywords: prime modifier highest attribute attack spell martial save DC awareness
entries.summary: Your Prime Modifier equals your highest Attribute.
entries.text: Prime is used for Attack Checks, Spell Checks, Martial Checks, Save DC, and Awareness. It changes whenever a different Attribute becomes your highest. Prime is not itself an Attribute, so effects that modify an Attribute do not automatically modify Prime-based rolls unless they change the highest value.
entries.title: Prime Modifier

entries.keywords: skill list mastery formula
entries.summary: Skills apply focused training to activities associated with an Attribute.
entries.text: Might governs Athletics and Intimidation. Agility governs Acrobatics, Trickery, and Stealth. Charisma governs Animal, Insight, and Influence. Intelligence governs Investigation, Medicine, and Survival. Awareness uses Prime. Make a Skill Check by rolling d20 + associated Attribute + Skill Mastery.
entries.title: Skills

entries.keywords: profession tools crafting knowledge artistry services subterfuge
entries.summary: Trades represent professional knowledge and the ability to perform specialized work.
entries.text: A Trade Check is d20 + an appropriate Attribute + Trade Mastery. Recalling information does not require tools, but performing a Trade normally requires its listed tools. Improvised tools impose DisADV. Variant Attributes can be used when the circumstances justify a different approach.
entries.title: Trades

entries.keywords: mortal exotic divine outer common language categories
entries.summary: Language Mastery determines whether you can read, write, speak, and understand a language.
entries.text: Mortal languages include Common and ancestry languages; Exotic includes Giant, Draconic, Fey, and Elemental; Divine includes Celestial and Fiendish; Outer includes Deep Speech. Characters begin Fluent in Common. Limited Mastery requires Language Checks, while Fluent Mastery does not.
entries.title: Languages

entries.keywords: novice adept expert master grandmaster mastery cap
entries.summary: Mastery measures competency in Skills, Trades, Languages, and Combat.
entries.text: Skill and Trade Mastery have five levels: Novice +2, Adept +4, Expert +6, Master +8, and Grandmaster +10. Normal caps are reached at character levels 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20. Language Mastery uses None, Limited, and Fluent. Combat Mastery equals half character level, rounded up.
entries.title: Mastery & Training

entries.keywords: skill points mastery limit expertise cap
entries.summary: Spend Skill Points to gain Skill Mastery or raise a specific Skill’s cap.
entries.text: Each Skill Mastery level grants +2. Background grants 5 Skill Points, modified by Intelligence; Classes and Talents can grant more. A Skill can benefit from only one bonus that raises its normal Mastery Limit. You can spend 1 Skill Point to raise a Skill’s cap by one and another point to raise its Mastery Level into that new cap.
entries.title: Skill Mastery

entries.id: Core Rules|Mastery & Training|Trade Mastery & Point Conversion
entries.keywords: trade points conversion skill point two trade points
entries.summary: Trade Points buy Trade Mastery, and Skill Points can be converted into Trade Points.
entries.text: Each Trade Mastery level grants +2 and follows the normal Mastery Limit. Background grants 3 Trade Points. Convert 1 Skill Point into 2 Trade Points, but not the reverse. A Trade can benefit from only one bonus that raises its normal Mastery Limit.
entries.title: Trade Mastery & Point Conversion

entries.id: Core Rules|Mastery & Training|Language Mastery & Point Conversion
entries.keywords: limited fluent trade point language point conversion
entries.summary: Limited Mastery permits Language Checks; Fluent Mastery permits normal use without a Check.
entries.text: Background grants Common Fluency and 2 Language Points. Convert 1 Trade Point into 2 Language Points, but not the reverse. Language Checks use d20 + Intelligence or Charisma. Suggested DCs are 10 for Mortal, 15 for Exotic or Divine, and 20 for Outer languages.
entries.title: Language Mastery & Point Conversion

entries.id: Core Rules|Mastery & Training|Combat Mastery & Combat Training
entries.keywords: CM training weapon armor shield spell focus
entries.summary: Combat Mastery scales with level; Combat Training determines whether equipment’s benefits can be used.
entries.text: Combat Mastery is half character level, rounded up, and applies to Attack and Spell Checks, PD and AD, Attribute Saves, and Save DC. Without Weapon Training you cannot use the Weapon Enhancement; without Spell Focus Training you do not gain focus properties; untrained Armor or Shields impose DisADV on Attack and Spell Checks.
entries.title: Combat Mastery & Combat Training

entries.keywords: check save contest willing fail
entries.summary: Checks initiate an attempt; Saves resist an effect imposed on you.
entries.text: Roll a d20 and add the bonuses specified by the roll. A willing creature can choose to fail, treating its result as 0 for degrees of success or failure without suffering a Critical Failure unless it chooses to. Contests are won by the higher result; a tie leaves the situation unchanged.
entries.title: Checks & Saves

entries.keywords: formula flat attack martial spell skill trade language
entries.summary: The roll’s type determines which Attribute and Mastery bonuses apply.
entries.text: Flat Attribute Check: d20 + Attribute. Attack, Spell, or Martial Check: d20 + Prime Modifier + Combat Mastery. Skill Check: d20 + Attribute + Skill Mastery. Trade Check: d20 + Attribute + Trade Mastery. Language Check: d20 + Intelligence or Charisma.
entries.title: Check Formulas

entries.id: Core Rules|Checks & Saves|Saves, Save Categories, & Save DC
entries.keywords: attribute physical mental death repeated save DC formula
entries.summary: Attribute Saves resist imposed effects; Physical and Mental Saves use the better of two Attribute Saves.
entries.text: Attribute Save: d20 + Attribute + Combat Mastery. Physical Save uses the better Might or Agility Save bonus. Mental Save uses the better Charisma or Intelligence Save bonus. Death Saves are a flat d20 against DC 10. Save DC equals 10 + Prime Modifier + Combat Mastery.
entries.title: Saves, Save Categories, & Save DC

entries.keywords: damage effect attack hit save failure simultaneous
entries.summary: Damage and an imposed effect resolve simultaneously with an Attack and a Save.
entries.text: The attacker’s Attack or Spell Check is compared with the target’s Defense to determine damage. At the same time, the target’s Save is compared with the attacker’s Save DC to determine the effect. Either, both, or neither part can succeed.
entries.title: Dynamic Attack Saves

entries.id: Core Rules|Checks & Saves|Checks Against Defenses, Saves, and DCs
entries.keywords: defense save DC multiple targets one check
entries.summary: Damage targets a Defense, hostile effects target a Save, and beneficial or self-directed effects target a DC.
entries.text: An Attack Check meets or exceeds PD or AD to deal damage. A hostile effect’s Check must be greater than the target’s Save. A Check against a static DC succeeds when it meets or exceeds the DC. One Check is normally used for all targets of the same action, and only one Save of each type is made against multiple same-type effects from that action.
entries.title: Checks Against Defenses, Saves, and DCs

entries.keywords: ADV DisADV stacking cancel highest lowest
entries.summary: ADV rolls extra d20s and keeps the highest; DisADV keeps the lowest.
entries.text: Each instance of ADV or DisADV adds one d20. ADV 2 rolls 3d20 and keeps the highest; DisADV 3 rolls 4d20 and keeps the lowest. Opposing instances cancel one-for-one. In Combat, AP can be spent to gain ADV on a Check or Save.
entries.title: Advantage & Disadvantage

entries.keywords: same check repeated multiple action penalty
entries.summary: Repeating the same type of Check during your turn adds stacking DisADV.
entries.text: The first attempt is normal, the second has DisADV 1, the third DisADV 2, and the fourth DisADV 3. The penalty applies only during the creature’s turn in Combat and does not normally affect Reactions on another creature’s turn.
entries.title: Multiple Check Penalty

entries.id: Core Rules|Advantage & Outcomes|Critical Outcomes & Degrees of Success
entries.keywords: critical success failure natural 20 natural 1 degrees by 5
entries.summary: Natural 20s and 1s create Critical outcomes; every 5 above or below a target can add effects.
entries.text: A natural 20 on a damaging Attack, Martial, or Spell Check is a Critical Hit: it automatically hits and deals +2 damage. A natural 1 automatically fails and leaves the creature Exposed to the next Attack before its next turn. Success (5), Success (10), Failure (5), Failure (10), and each-5 statements scale from the difference between the result and target.
entries.title: Critical Outcomes & Degrees of Success

entries.keywords: melee ranged area close quarters long range
entries.summary: Martial and Spell Attacks can be Melee, Ranged, or Area Attacks.
entries.text: Melee Range is normally 1 Space. Ranged Attacks use their listed range and have DisADV while the attacker is within an enemy’s Melee Range. Weapon long-range Attacks have DisADV and cannot exceed long range. Area Attacks affect creatures inside the specified area and ignore the Close Quarters penalty.
entries.title: Attacks & Attack Ranges

entries.id: Core Rules|Attacks & Defenses|Precision Defense & Area Defense
entries.keywords: PD AD defense formula agility intelligence might charisma
entries.summary: PD avoids precise attacks; AD withstands attacks that cover an area.
entries.text: PD = 8 + Combat Mastery + Agility + Intelligence + bonuses. AD = 8 + Combat Mastery + Might + Charisma + bonuses. Armor, Shields, Ancestry Traits, Class Features, and other effects can modify these values.
entries.title: Precision Defense & Area Defense

entries.id: Core Rules|Health & Damage|Health, Temporary HP, & Thresholds
entries.keywords: HP temporary bloodied well-bloodied death threshold
entries.summary: HP measures how much punishment a creature can sustain; thresholds mark increasingly dangerous states.
entries.text: Starting HP = Class HP + Might + Ancestry HP. Temporary HP absorbs damage first, does not stack, and normally ends on a Long Rest. Bloodied is at half maximum HP or lower; Well-Bloodied is at one quarter or lower; Death’s Door begins at 0 HP. Death Threshold equals 0 - Prime Modifier - Combat Mastery.
entries.title: Health, Temporary HP, & Thresholds

entries.id: Core Rules|Health & Damage|Death’s Door & Death Saves
entries.keywords: death save bleeding unconscious zero HP
entries.summary: A PC at 0 HP remains conscious but is severely limited and at risk of death.
entries.text: Entering Death’s Door gives Exhaustion 1 and reduces current and maximum AP by 3 until HP returns to 1 or higher. At the start of each turn, make a DC 10 Death Save. Success (5) restores 1 HP; Critical Success restores the PC to 1 HP. Failure gives Bleeding 1; Failure (5) gives Bleeding 2; Critical Failure also causes Unconsciousness.
entries.title: Death’s Door & Death Saves

entries.id: Core Rules|Health & Damage|Damage, Heavy Hits, & Critical Hits
entries.keywords: heavy hit brutal hit critical hit damage
entries.summary: Attacks gain +1 damage for every 5 the Check exceeds the target’s Defense.
entries.text: Meeting Defense is a Hit for base damage. Five over is a Heavy Hit for +1; ten over is a Brutal Hit for +2. A natural 20 is a Critical Hit, automatically hits, bypasses Damage Reduction, and adds +2 damage in addition to any damage gained from exceeding Defense.
entries.title: Damage, Heavy Hits, & Critical Hits

entries.id: Core Rules|Health & Damage|Damage Types, Resistance, & Damage Reduction
entries.keywords: physical elemental mystical true PDR EDR MDR vulnerability immunity resistance
entries.summary: Damage is Physical, Elemental, Mystical, or True and can be modified by Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, and DR.
entries.text: Physical: Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing. Elemental: Cold, Corrosion, Fire, Lightning, Poison. Mystical: Psychic, Radiant, Umbral. True damage cannot be reduced. Resistance X subtracts X; Resistance Half halves damage; Immunity reduces it to 0; Vulnerability X adds X; Vulnerability Double doubles it. PDR, EDR, and MDR grant Resistance Half against qualifying Attacks except Critical and Heavy Hits or higher.
entries.title: Damage Types, Resistance, & Damage Reduction

entries.keywords: skill check Might
entries.summary: Might Skill
entries.text:
Athletics covers activities that involve physical prowess, such as climbing, swimming, and jumping in difficult circumstances, or participating in a Grapple.

Climbing: Attempting to climb a sheer or slippery surface, or cling to one.

Swimming: Attempting to swim in treacherous waters or a viscous liquid.

Jumping: Attempting to jump a distance that exceeds your Jump Distance.

Grappling: Attempting to Grapple another creature or avoid being Grappled by one.
entries.title: Athletics

entries.keywords: skill check Might
entries.summary: Might Skill
entries.text:
Intimidation covers attempts to influence a creature's behavior using threats, hostile actions, and physical violence.

Threaten Violence: Attempting to scare someone into doing something... or else.

Forceful Command: Attempting to boss someone around with your intimidating strength.
entries.title: Intimidation

entries.keywords: skill check Agility
entries.summary: Agility Skill
entries.text:
Acrobatics covers activities that require flexibility, nimbleness, and balance.

Balance: Attempting to maintain your balance in tricky situations, such as walking across a slippery surface, staying upright on a rocking boat, or balancing on a tightrope.

Jumping: Attempting to jump a distance that exceeds your Jump Distance.

Stunts: Attempting to perform a stunt that requires flexibility or being nimble, such as aerial maneuvers, dives, rolls, somersaults, or flips.
entries.title: Acrobatics

entries.keywords: skill check Agility
entries.summary: Agility Skill
entries.text:
Trickery covers non-verbal means of deceiving others, such as pickpocketing things, concealing an object on your person, or other forms of physical deception.

Sleight of Hand: Attempting to pocket something from another person or plant something on them.

Forgery: Attempting to create fake documents that appear to be legitimate.

Conceal Object: Attempting to manipulate or hide an object somewhere out of sight. This could be in your hand, up your sleeve, on a person, or in another object.

Traps: Attempting to deploy or disarm a trap or similar device with steady hands.
entries.title: Trickery

entries.keywords: skill check Agility
entries.summary: Agility Skill
entries.text:
Stealth covers attempts to avoid being seen or heard by other creatures, such as sneaking about or hiding behind cover. These Checks occur during the moment of possible discovery when a creature might be heard or seen.

Sneaking: Attempting to move about quietly to avoid being noticed by other creatures.

Hiding: Attempting to Hide from a creature so that they can't see you.
entries.title: Stealth

entries.keywords: skill check Charisma
entries.summary: Charisma Skill
entries.text:
Animal covers interactions such as corralling, training, calming, and gauging the intention of Beasts.

Calming: Attempting to soothe a startled Beast or make it feel safe.

Communicate: Attempting to train, domesticate, or command a wild Beast.
entries.title: Animal

entries.keywords: skill check Charisma
entries.summary: Charisma Skill
entries.text:
Insight governs your ability to discern intentions. This could be from observing a creature's body language, facial cues, and mannerisms. Alternatively, Insight can represent a gut feeling or intuition about a situation.

Discern Intent: Attempting to determine if a creature's behavior is reflective of it being truthful, deceptive, or hiding something.

Evaluate Threat: Attempting to see if a threat from a creature is a bluff or real.
entries.title: Insight

entries.keywords: skill check Charisma
entries.summary: Charisma Skill
entries.text:
Influence covers your attempts to manipulate a creature's behavior using compelling arguments based on truth, half-truths, lies, or some combination in between.

Convince: Attempting to get people to do what you want with truth or lies.

Mislead: Attempting to make false claims, accusations, or promises that you don't intend to keep.

Inspire: Attempting to give a speech to a person or group to encourage them.

Negotiate: Attempting to socially barter for peace or hostility between factions.
entries.title: Influence

entries.keywords: skill check Intelligence
entries.summary: Intelligence Skill
entries.text:
Investigation covers using your senses to search for and discover things that are not readily observable. You look for clues and then make deductions on those clues to try to discern the locations of things or how they work, such as finding hidden objects, secret doors, or weak points in structures. It also covers the process of researching information through various texts.

Searching & Discovery: Attempting to find something that is not able to be seen from afar, then deduce how it works, such as a trap.

Analysis & Research: Attempting to pore through scrolls, manuscripts, or books for information and hidden knowledge.
entries.title: Investigation

entries.keywords: skill check Intelligence
entries.summary: Intelligence Skill
entries.text:
Medicine covers activities that involve medical knowledge and application, such as treating a wounded creature, diagnosing an illness, or identifying a cure to an ailment.

Treat Wound: Attempting to mend or stabilize a wounded creature.

Diagnose Cause: Attempting to discern the cause or cure of a poison, disease, or injury.

Forensics: Attempting to determine the cause or time of a creature's death.
entries.title: Medicine

entries.keywords: skill check Intelligence
entries.summary: Intelligence Skill
entries.text:
Survival covers the activities required to survive in the wilderness, such as tracking quarry, foraging for food and water, and navigating through uncharted territory.

Tracking & Foraging: Attempting to find the location of a creature, food, or water in the area.

Hunting: Attempting to harvest materials from slain creatures, including extracting poisons, removing carapaces, and skinning pelts.

Navigation: Attempting to navigate through uncharted territory. This can determine which paths lead to a chosen destination, avoid natural hazards such as quicksand, identify evidence of creatures that inhabit the area, or predict the weather within the area for the next 24 hours.
entries.title: Survival

entries.keywords: skill check Prime
entries.summary: Prime Skill
entries.text:
Awareness governs your ability to detect the presence of other creatures or objects using your sight, hearing, smell, or other senses. You can attempt to detect a creature that's visible, making noise, giving off a distinct smell, or otherwise causing a disturbance in the environment, such as causing the ground to shake, the water to ripple, or the air to blow.

See: Attempting to spot something easy to miss, such as miscreants hiding in the shadows of an alley or candlelight under a closed secret door.

Hear: Attempting to listen to a conversation through a closed door, around a corner, or under an open window.

Smell: Attempting to smell an odd or recognizable scent on a creature or somewhere nearby.
entries.title: Awareness

entries.keywords: trade check Agility Calligrapher's Supplies
entries.summary: Agility • Calligrapher's Supplies
entries.text:
Illustration is the ability to put ink or paint to paper to create beautiful art in drawings, paintings, and calligraphy.

Drawing: Creating images by making marks and lines with a pen on paper.

Calligraphy: Creating visually ornate handwritten lettering.

Painting: Creating images by putting paint on a surface, usually with a brush.

Tool: Calligrapher's Supplies
entries.title: Illustration

entries.keywords: trade check Agility or Charisma Musical Instrument
entries.summary: Agility or Charisma • Musical Instrument
entries.text:
Musicians are skilled in the use of a variety of instruments, which they can use to make impressive performances of sound.

Bagpipe: A bag set with pipes that creates musical sounds when squeezed, as wind escapes through the pipes.

Drum: An instrument that's sounded by being struck with hands or sticks.

Flute: An instrument made from a tube with holes in it, played by blowing into the tube and covering different holes to create musical notes.

Harp: A stringed instrument with a somewhat triangular frame, played by plucking its strings by hand.

Horn: A tube-like instrument, played by using one's mouth to blow air through the instrument.

Lute: A stringed instrument with a long neck, played by putting fingers on frets and plucking strings to create musical notes.

Piano: An instrument with a large frame that encases a board of metal strings that creates sound when keys are pressed, as hammers strike the strings.

Tool: Musical Instrument
entries.title: Musician

entries.keywords: trade check Charisma None
entries.summary: Charisma • None
entries.text:
Theatre is the art of expressive performance, through acting, dancing, singing, or even juggling or other dazzling displays.

Acting: A performance done by embodying someone or something else, pretending you are them.

Comedy: A humorous performance done to make others smile and laugh.

Dancing: A visual performance done by moving one's body in eye-catching and provocative ways.

Singing: A performance using one's voice to create music.

Storytelling: A performance of vivid words to create a narrative that evokes powerful emotions and insights.

Juggling: A performance done by continuously throwing objects into the air and catching them while keeping at least one in the air while handling the others.

Tool: None
entries.title: Theatre

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence or Agility Alchemist's Supplies
entries.summary: Intelligence or Agility • Alchemist's Supplies
entries.text:
Alchemy is the practice of creating something by combining or changing other things, such as creating magical potions or changing one element into another.

Magic Potions: Alchemical potions can have all manner of magical effects with extreme versatility.

Transmuting Elements: It's possible to transform lead into gold, water into wine, or blood into acid using alchemy.

Tool: Alchemist's Supplies
entries.title: Alchemy

entries.keywords: trade check Might Blacksmith's Tools
entries.summary: Might • Blacksmith's Tools
entries.text:
Blacksmithing is the practice of melting and shaping metal into objects, such as nails, horse shoes, or armor and weapons.

Metal Armor: Armor made from metal, such as chain, splint, and plate mail.

Metal Weapons: Weapons made from metal, such as axes, daggers, and swords.

Tool: Blacksmith's Tools
entries.title: Blacksmithing

entries.keywords: trade check Agility or Might Glassblower's Tools
entries.summary: Agility or Might • Glassblower's Tools
entries.text:
Glassblowing is the practice of blowing molten sand into glass objects, such as cups, bowls, vases, ornaments, lenses, window panes, and other objects.

Tool: Glassblower's Tools
entries.title: Glassblowing

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence Herbalist's Supplies
entries.summary: Intelligence • Herbalist's Supplies
entries.text:
Herbalism is the practice of combining various mundane plants to create concoctions that can be used to treat afflictions, heal wounds, or poison enemies.

Brews: Teas, tonics, and tinctures are types of brews you can drink.

Ointments: Infusions, balms, and salves are types of ointments you can apply to your skin.

Bandages: A poultice is a type of bandage that you apply over a wound with a wrapping.

Medicine & Poison: Herbalism is normally used to create medicines; however, any medicine delivered with a very high dosage can be poisonous. The reverse is also true: many poisons are used as medicines in very small dosages.

Tool: Herbalist's Supplies
entries.title: Herbalism

entries.keywords: trade check Agility Jeweler's Tools
entries.summary: Agility • Jeweler's Tools
entries.text:
Jewelers can beautify, identify, and even price various gems, stones, and jewelry, and can identify magical gems or the magical uses of mundane gems.

Tool: Jeweler's Tools
entries.title: Jeweler

entries.keywords: trade check Agility Leatherworker's Tools
entries.summary: Agility • Leatherworker's Tools
entries.text:
Leatherworking is the practice of making leather from animal skins or making leather into usable items, such as clothing, armor, weapon sheaths, and other objects.

Tool: Leatherworker's Tools
entries.title: Leatherworking

entries.keywords: trade check Agility Sculptor's Tools
entries.summary: Agility • Sculptor's Tools
entries.text:
Sculpting is the practice of shaping bone, clay, glass, stone, or wood into figures, tools, idols, or simple weapons.

Containers: Cups, bowls, plates, and vases.

Figures: Statues of creatures or objects, such as mortals, deities, animals, and buildings.

Weapons: Simple weapons, such as knives, clubs, and arrows.

Trinkets: Small idols, animals, and symbols.

Tool: Sculptor's Tools
entries.title: Sculpting

entries.keywords: trade check Agility or Intelligence Tinkerer's Tools
entries.summary: Agility or Intelligence • Tinkerer's Tools
entries.text:
Tinkering is the practice of making, repairing, or operating mechanisms, such as traps and clockwork devices.

Traps: Setting up and disarming traps requires the use of specialized tools, such as Tinkerer's Tools, to manipulate its arming mechanisms.

Clockwork Devices: Clockwork devices operate using a series of intricate mechanisms, such as gears, springs, and levers. The devices can be tuned, modified, or repaired using Tinkerer's Tools.

Tool: Tinkerer's Tools
entries.title: Tinkering

entries.keywords: trade check Agility Weaver's Tools
entries.summary: Agility • Weaver's Tools
entries.text:
Weaving is the practice of creating material for clothing or using such material to create clothes, curtains, tapestries, and other woven objects.

Tool: Weaver's Tools
entries.title: Weaving

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence None
entries.summary: Intelligence • None
entries.text:
Arcane knowledge encompasses the study of arcane magic, the planes of existence, and the underlying principles that govern reality beyond mundane understanding.

It can be used to recall information about arcane magic, spells, items, runes, glyphs, and symbols; creatures such as Constructs, Monstrosities, and Oozes; and planes of existence and the creatures who inhabit those planes.

Tool: None
entries.title: Arcana

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence None
entries.summary: Intelligence • None
entries.text:
Engineering represents a character's understanding of mechanics, construction, and the application of scientific principles in a world that blends magic and technology.

It can be used for designing and operating gears, pulleys, mechanical engines, and motors, and for understanding the architecture of buildings, bridges, tunnels, and fortresses.

Tool: None
entries.title: Engineering

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence None
entries.summary: Intelligence • None
entries.text:
History involves the study of past events, including recorded events and ancient lore, and provides insight into how civilizations, cultures, and legends have shaped the present world.

It can be used to recall historical events, conflicts, and wars; creatures such as Dragons, Giants, and Humanoids; and lost civilizations, kingdoms, and legends.

Tool: None
entries.title: History

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence None
entries.summary: Intelligence • None
entries.text:
Nature represents a character's understanding of the natural world, including the elements, weather patterns, and magical and mundane ecosystems.

It can be used to recall Primal and Elemental magic, including earth, fire, water, air, and lightning magic; creatures such as Beasts, Elementals, Fey, and Plants; and natural parts of the world such as terrain, weather, seasons, and natural disasters.

Tool: None
entries.title: Nature

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence None
entries.summary: Intelligence • None
entries.text:
Occultism represents a character's understanding of forbidden magic, secret cults, and the dealings of sinister creatures.

It can be used to recall unholy magic and knowledge of the forbidden; creatures such as Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead; and the practices of secret cults and the signs of their presence.

Tool: None
entries.title: Occultism

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence None
entries.summary: Intelligence • None
entries.text:
Religion represents a character's understanding of divine magic, deities, and religious organizations.

It can be used to recall holy magic, relics, auras, and symbols; creatures such as Deities, Celestials, and Angels; and religious rites, prayers, hierarchies, and practices.

Tool: None
entries.title: Religion

entries.keywords: trade check Agility, Intelligence, or Charisma Brewer's Supplies
entries.summary: Agility, Intelligence, or Charisma • Brewer's Supplies
entries.text:
Brewing is the practice of producing alcohol, especially beer, mead, and wine.

Tool: Brewer's Supplies
entries.title: Brewing

entries.keywords: trade check Agility or Might Carpenter's Tools
entries.summary: Agility or Might • Carpenter's Tools
entries.text:
Carpentry is the practice of measuring, cutting, and installing pieces of wood to create structures that form buildings, bridges, ships, and other large structures.

Tool: Carpenter's Tools
entries.title: Carpentry

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence or Agility Cartographer's Tools
entries.summary: Intelligence or Agility • Cartographer's Tools
entries.text:
Cartography is the practice of drawing and understanding maps.

Tool: Cartographer's Tools
entries.title: Cartography

entries.keywords: trade check Agility, Intelligence, or Charisma Cooking Utensils
entries.summary: Agility, Intelligence, or Charisma • Cooking Utensils
entries.text:
Cooking is the practice of preparing, mixing, and heating edible ingredients to create meals.

Tool: Cooking Utensils
entries.title: Cooking

entries.keywords: trade check Might Mason's Tools
entries.summary: Might • Mason's Tools
entries.text:
Masonry is the practice of working and installing stone into structures that form buildings, bridges, furnaces, and other large structures.

Tool: Mason's Tools
entries.title: Masonry

entries.keywords: trade check Agility, Intelligence, or Might Vehicle required
entries.summary: Agility, Intelligence, or Might • Vehicle required
entries.text:
Vehicles covers the practice of managing, operating, and steering vehicles, whether on land, sea, or air.

Water Vehicles: Boats, canoes, kayaks, and large ships.

Air Vehicles: Airships and Astral Jumpers used for space travel.

Land Vehicles: Clockwork or other magical land vehicles.

Tool: Vehicle required
entries.title: Vehicles

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence Cryptographer's Tools
entries.summary: Intelligence • Cryptographer's Tools
entries.text:
Cryptography is the process of converting messages into secret or disguised words to protect them from being understood. The message must be deciphered to discern its true meaning.

Tool: Cryptographer's Tools
entries.title: Cryptography

entries.keywords: trade check Agility or Charisma Disguise Kit
entries.summary: Agility or Charisma • Disguise Kit
entries.text:
The art of disguise is the ability to alter one's appearance to conceal identity or appear as someone else.

Tool: Disguise Kit
entries.title: Disguise

entries.keywords: trade check Intelligence or Charisma Gaming Set
entries.summary: Intelligence or Charisma • Gaming Set
entries.text:
Gaming is the practice of playing games skillfully, for money or for entertainment.

Dice: Cubes with pips on each side to denote a number, rolled to randomly get one such number in games of chance.

Playing Cards: Small pieces of paper that each have an image that denotes a value, shuffled and given randomly in games of chance.

Gambling: Playing games of chance to earn money.

Tool: Gaming Set
entries.title: Gaming

entries.keywords: trade check Agility or Intelligence Lockpicking Tools
entries.summary: Agility or Intelligence • Lockpicking Tools
entries.text:
Lockpicking is the practice of opening devices secured by interworking mechanisms, such as locks and traps.

Locks: Lockpicking is the ability to open a lock without the proper key, usually using thin instruments to force a lock open from within by rotating tumblers and listening for the proper sounds. A lock's key can also be copied using specialized tools while studying the lock.

Traps: Setting up and disarming traps requires specialized tools, such as Tinkerer's Tools, to manipulate its arming mechanisms.

Tool: Lockpicking Tools
entries.title: Lockpicking

entries.summary: Action economy, martial and spellcasting systems, and alternating initiative.
entries.text: Combat Rules explains how AP, MP, SP, and Grit power actions; how Maneuvers and Spells work; and how an encounter begins and proceeds. Use the topic selector to jump directly to Actions, Maneuvers, Spellcasting, Spells, or Initiative.
entries.title: Combat Rules Overview

entries.keywords: AP four refresh action reaction
entries.summary: Every creature normally has a maximum of 4 AP for Actions and Reactions.
entries.text: Spend AP to take Actions, Reactions, and Enhancements. Once spent, AP remains spent until regained at the end of your turn. AP spent on Reactions before your turn reduces the AP available during that turn. Outside Combat, the GM controls pacing and AP is not normally tracked.
entries.title: Action Points

entries.id: Combat Rules|Combat Resources|Mana Points & Mana Spend Limit
entries.keywords: MP MSL spellcaster long rest
entries.summary: MP powers magical effects and normally returns only after a Long Rest.
entries.text: Spellcasting Classes and the Spellcaster Path grant MP. Mana Spend Limit equals Combat Mastery and caps the MP that can be spent on one effect, including Enhancements. All spent MP returns after a Long Rest.
entries.title: Mana Points & Mana Spend Limit

entries.id: Combat Rules|Combat Resources|Stamina Points & Stamina Spend Limit
entries.keywords: SP SSL martial stamina regen short rest
entries.summary: SP powers martial effects and can be recovered during or after Combat.
entries.text: Martial Classes and the Martial Path grant SP. Stamina Spend Limit equals Combat Mastery and caps the SP spent on one effect, including Enhancements. All SP returns when Combat ends and after a Short Rest; each Martial Class has a Stamina Regen method for recovery during Combat.
entries.title: Stamina Points & Stamina Spend Limit

entries.keywords: grit charisma damage reduction save advantage
entries.summary: Grit equals 2 + Charisma, minimum 0, and represents force of will.
entries.text: When Hit, spend Grit to reduce damage by 1 per point. Before rolling a Save, spend Grit to gain ADV on that Save. All Grit returns after a Long Rest.
entries.title: Grit Points

entries.keywords: minor action draw sheathe item door
entries.summary: Anything that spends AP is an Action; two simple item interactions can be Minor Actions each turn.
entries.text: Spend the AP listed in an Action to take it. Once per turn, perform up to two Minor Action tasks without AP, with no Action between them: open or close a door, grab or release an item, retrieve or stow an item, or draw or sheathe a Weapon. Spend 1 AP for another Minor Action that turn.
entries.title: Actions & Minor Actions

entries.keywords: attack disarm grapple shove tackle
entries.summary: Attack, Disarm, Grapple, Shove, and Tackle directly pressure opponents.
entries.text: Attack spends 1 AP for one Attack Check. Disarm contests an Attack Check against Athletics, Acrobatics, or Trickery. Grapple uses a free hand and contests Athletics against Athletics or Acrobatics. Shove contests Athletics and pushes 1 Space plus 1 per Success (each 5), with the option to trade 1 Space for Prone. Tackle follows a 2-Space approach and can Grapple and knock both creatures Prone.
entries.title: Offensive Actions

entries.keywords: disengage full dodge hide stealth passive awareness
entries.summary: Disengage, Dodge, and Hide reduce danger or prevent enemies from finding you.
entries.text: Disengage spends 1 AP to impose DisADV on Opportunity Attacks; Full Disengage spends 1 more AP for immunity. Dodge spends 1 AP to impose DisADV on the next Attack or Grapple; Full Dodge spends 1 more AP to affect all until your next turn. Hide spends 1 AP for Stealth against Passive Awareness while Unseen.
entries.title: Defensive Actions

entries.keywords: move help d8 object spell sustain dazed
entries.summary: Move, Help, Object, Spell, and Sustained Actions handle positioning, teamwork, and ongoing effects.
entries.text: Move spends 1 AP to gain movement equal to Speed and can be split around other Actions. Help spends 1 AP to grant a d8 Help Die to a declared Attack, Skill, or Trade Check; repeated Help Actions decay the die toward d4. Object spends 1 AP for an involved item interaction. Spell spends its listed AP and MP. Sustained effects require 1 AP at the start of each turn and end if the creature becomes Dazed.
entries.title: Utility Actions

entries.keywords: analyze calm animal insight conceal feint intimidate investigate medicine search taunt
entries.summary: Combat makes direct use of Skills through defined one-AP Actions.
entries.text: Analyze Creature recalls lore and statistics. Calm Animal, Combat Insight, Conceal, Feint, Intimidate, Investigate, Extend Jump, Medicine, Mounted Defense, Pass Through, Search, and Taunt each specify a Skill Check, target, and outcome. Their degrees of success can add information, movement, healing, or stronger Conditions.
entries.title: Skill-Based Actions

entries.keywords: ready hold trigger interrupt reaction
entries.summary: Spend AP now and declare an Action plus an observable Trigger to act later as a Reaction.
entries.text: The declared Action and Trigger cannot be changed. If the Trigger occurs before the start of your next turn, perform the Action as a Reaction and pay any additional resources then. The Reaction interrupts the Trigger. If the Trigger never occurs or the Action cannot be completed, its AP is wasted.
entries.title: Held Actions

entries.keywords: trigger prerequisite AP multiple reactions
entries.summary: Reactions are Actions taken on another creature’s turn and spend the same AP pool.
entries.text: A Reaction requires its Prerequisite and Trigger, and only one Reaction can be taken for each Trigger. Reactions ignore the Multiple Check Penalty. Multiple Reactions are possible when different Triggers occur and the creature has enough resources.
entries.title: Reactions

entries.keywords: opportunity attack leaving reach draw object
entries.summary: Martial Path creatures can punish specific actions within Melee Range.
entries.text: Trigger: a visible creature within your Melee Range uses movement to leave your reach, draws a Weapon or Spell Focus, picks up an item, or takes the Object Action. Spend 1 AP as a Reaction to make a Melee Martial Attack against it.
entries.title: Opportunity Attacks

entries.keywords: counterspell caster challenger MP contest
entries.summary: A Spellcaster Path creature can challenge a visible MP Effect as it is cast.
entries.text: When the Caster or a target is within 5 Spaces, spend AP equal to the effect’s base AP cost and at least 1 MP. The Challenger and Caster contest Spell Checks, each adding twice the MP they spent for the duel. Combo Spellcasting allows additional creatures to assist either side.
entries.title: Spell Duels

entries.keywords: martial maneuver enhancement attack defense grapple utility combo
entries.summary: Martial characters spend SP to perform Maneuvers and can enhance them within the Stamina Spend Limit.
entries.text: Maneuvers list an AP and SP cost, range, requirements, effect, and possible Enhancements. Maneuver Enhancements modify a specific Maneuver; Martial Enhancements can be added to qualifying Martial Attacks. Categories are Attack, Defense, Grapple, and Utility. Advanced and Combo Maneuvers introduce additional timing and teamwork rules.
entries.title: Maneuvers

entries.keywords: cast spell components verbal somatic mana spend limit
entries.summary: Spellcasters use known Spells, their Spell List, AP, and MP to produce magical effects.
entries.text: A Spell lists source, school, tags, AP and MP cost, range, duration, description, and Enhancements. Casting must satisfy any Verbal and Somatic Components. MP spent on the Spell and its Enhancements cannot exceed Mana Spend Limit. Spells without MP costs can still receive qualifying Enhancements.
entries.title: Spellcasting

entries.id: Combat Rules|Spellcasting - Rules|Spell Sources, Schools, & Tags
entries.keywords: arcane divine primal astromancy conjuration divination elemental enchantment invocation nullification transmutation
entries.summary: Spell Lists are defined through Sources of Magic, Schools, and descriptive Tags.
entries.text: Sources are Arcane, Divine, and Primal. Schools are Astromancy, Conjuration, Divination, Elemental, Enchantment, Invocation, Nullification, and Transmutation. Tags describe shared mechanics or themes and determine whether a Feature can interact with a Spell.
entries.title: Spell Sources, Schools, & Tags

entries.id: Combat Rules|Advanced Spellcasting|Combo Spellcasting & Wild Magic
entries.keywords: combo casting participant wild magic
entries.summary: Multiple Spellcasters can combine magic, while unstable casting can invoke Wild Magic.
entries.text: Combo Spellcasting lets Participants assist a primary Caster by contributing permitted resources and Checks. During a Spell Duel, assistants can help either Caster or Challenger. Wild Magic uses the table when a rule instructs the Caster to trigger a Wild Magic result.
entries.title: Combo Spellcasting & Wild Magic

entries.id: Combat Rules|Starting Combat|Starting Combat & Encounter DC
entries.keywords: initiative check encounter DC surprise
entries.summary: The GM establishes the encounter, determines Encounter DC, and calls for team Initiative.
entries.text: Each PC makes Initiative using d20 + Agility + Combat Mastery against the Encounter DC. If at least half succeed, the PC team takes the first Initiative Turn; otherwise the enemy team does. Surprise and encounter circumstances can modify starting resources or positioning.
entries.title: Starting Combat & Encounter DC

entries.keywords: round turn order team initiative alternate
entries.summary: PC and enemy Initiative Turns alternate whenever possible.
entries.text: On a team’s Initiative Turn, that team chooses an eligible creature to take its turn. Once every creature has acted, a new Round begins and eligibility resets. Team turns alternate until one side has no eligible creatures remaining, after which the other side resolves its remaining turns.
entries.title: Alternating Initiative

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Weapon or Unarmed Strike
entries.text:
The force of your Attack pushes the target away. Make a Melee Martial Attack against the PD of a target within range, and it makes a Might Save against your Save DC. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike. Save Failure: The target is pushed 1 Space away from you. Save Failure (each 5): The target is pushed up to 1 additional Space. Knock Prone: After the result, you can choose to reduce the total distance a target is pushed by 1 Space to knock them Prone instead.

Airborne: When you choose to push them upward into the air, the distance they’re pushed is halved.

Enhancements
Increased Distance: (X SP) The distance pushed increases by X Spaces. Bowling Ball: (1 SP) If the target collides with another creature as part of this movement, the creature it collides with must make a Might Save against your Save DC. Save Failure: The target is knocked Prone. Save Failure (each 5): The target is also pushed 1 Space away from you.
entries.title: Heroic Bash

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Weapon or Unarmed Strike
entries.text:
You cause a creature to bleed with the ferocity and precision of your attack. Make a Martial Attack against the PD of a target within range, and it makes a Repeated Physical Save against your Save DC. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike. Save Failure: The target becomes Impaired or begins Bleeding (your choice) for 1 minute.

Enhancements
Improved Bleed: (X SP) On a failed Save, the target gains Bleeding X for the duration. Improved Impaired: (X SP) On a failed Save, the target gains Impaired X for the duration. Weakened: (2 SP) On a failed Save, the target is Weakened for the duration.
entries.title: Savage Strike

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 1 AP + 2 SP • Weapon or Unarmed Strike
entries.text:
You make a target vulnerable to Physical damage. Make a Martial Attack against the PD of a target within range, and it makes a Physical Save against your Save DC. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike. Save Failure: The target gains Physical Vulnerability (1) for 1 Round.

Enhancements
Improved Vulnerability: (2 SP, Repeatable) Vulnerability increases by 1.

The

Break DR: (1 SP) On a failed Save, the target doesn’t benefit from PDR for the duration. Break Resistance: (2 SP) On a failed Save, the target doesn’t benefit from Physical Resistance for the duration.
entries.title: Sunder Strike

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Weapon or Unarmed Strike
entries.text:
You move around the area, attacking 1 creature you pass along the way. You move a number of Spaces up to your Speed and make a Melee Martial Attack against the PD of 1 target within your Melee Range at any point during this movement. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike.

Enhancements
Disengage: (1 SP) This movement doesn’t provoke Opportunity Attacks. Subsequent Strike: (1 AP + 1 SP, Repeatable) You gain additional movement equal to half your Speed and you can target an additional creature using the same Attack Check.
entries.title: Swift Strike

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Weapon or Unarmed Strike
entries.text:
A mid-air strike.

Your Jump Distance increases by 2, you Jump up to your Jump Distance without spending movement (provided you can move), and make a Melee Martial Attack against a target within range at any point during your jump or where you land. Reaction: You can spend an additional 1 SP to perform this Maneuver as a Reaction to a creature entering a Space within your Jump Distance that’s at least 1 Space above the ground. DC Tip: Remember, your Long Jump Distance equals your Jump Distance in Spaces, and your High Jump distance equals your Jump Distance in feet.

Enhancements
Falling Strike: (1 SP) The creature makes a Physical Save against your Save DC. Save Failure: The creature falls Prone. Slam Down: (1 SP, Requires Falling Strike) On a failed Save, the target doesn’t benefit from any ability that prevents it from falling as a result of being knocked Prone in midair until the end of the turn. Impact Crater: (1 AP + 1 SP) All creatures within a 1 Space aura of where you land must make a Physical Save against your Save DC. Save Failure: The creature falls Prone. Larger Crater: (2 SP, Repeatable, Requires Impact Crater) The size of the Aura increases by 1.
entries.title: Meteor Strike

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 2 AP • 2 Space Arc (Self)
entries.text:
You swing wide to attack targets around you. Make an Area Martial Attack against the AD of every target within range. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike. Reach Weapon: If you have a Reach Weapon, you can extend the Point of Origin 1 Space away from you. The Arc must still be facing away from you.

Enhancements
Damage: (2 SP, Repeatable) The damage increases by 1. Area: (2 SP, Repeatable) The Arc increases by 1 Space. Careful Cleave: (X SP) You can choose X targets in the area to avoid with the Attack. Sweep: (2 SP) Each target makes an Agility Save. Save Failure: The target is knocked Prone.
entries.title: Cleave

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 2 AP • 1 Space Aura
entries.text:
You attack in a circle around you, attacking everyone within range. Make an Area Martial Attack using a Melee Weapon or Unarmed Strike against the AD of every target within range. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike. Reach Weapon: If you have a Reach Weapon, you can choose to increase the Aura by 1 Space. When you do, you can’t Attack targets within 1 Space of you.

Enhancements
Damage: (2 SP, Repeatable) The damage increases by 1. Area: (2 SP, Repeatable) The Aura increases by 1 Space. Vortex: (2 SP, Repeatable) Each target makes a Might Save. Save Failure: The target is pushed up to 1 Space horizontally in a direction of your choice. The target is moved 1 additional Space each time you use this Enhancement.
entries.title: Whirlwind

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 2 AP • 4 Space Line (Self)
entries.text:
You attack every creature in a line. Make an Area Martial Attack with a Melee Weapon or Unarmed Strike against the AD of every target in a 4 Space Line. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon or Unarmed Strike. After Attacking, you can move to any Space within 1 Space of the area without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the targets and without spending your movement. Reach Weapon: If you have a Reach Weapon, you can extend the Point of Origin 1 Space away from you. When you do, the Line must extend in a direction away from you.

Enhancements
Damage: (2 SP, Repeatable) The damage increases by 1. Increase Length: (1 SP, Repeatable) The length of the Line increases by 2 Spaces. Carved Path: (2 SP, Repeatable) Each target makes a Might Save. Save Failure: The target is pushed 1 Space horizontallyout of the area in a direction of your choice. The target is moved 1 additional Space each time you use this Enhancement.
entries.title: Pathcarver

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 2 AP • Ranged Weapon or Weapon with the Toss or Thrown Property
entries.text:
You fire a powerful shot that pierces through creatures in a line. Make an Area Martial Attack against the AD of every target within a 8 Space Line that’s Point of Origin is within Range. The Line must extend away from you. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon. Close Quarters Penalty: You have DisADV on the Attack if you’re within the Melee Range of at least 1 enemy, unless that enemy is Incapacitated. DC Tip: Remember, you have DisADV on any Attack beyond your Weapon’s Normal Range.

Enhancements
Damage: (2 SP, Repeatable) The damage increases by 1. Area: (1 SP, Repeatable) The length of the Line increases by 4 Spaces. Penetrating Shot: (1 SP) The Attack ignores Cover but is blocked by 6 inches (15 cm) of wood or soft earth (dirt, mud, or sand), or 1 inch (25 mm) of metal or rock.
entries.title: Piercing Shot

entries.keywords: Attack Ranged Weapon
entries.summary: 2 AP • Self • Requirement: Ranged Weapon
entries.text:
You unleash a cone of projectiles. Make an Area Martial Attack against the AD of every target within a 3 Space Cone. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon.

Enhancements
Damage: (2 SP, Repeatable) The damage increases by 1. Area: (2 SP, Repeatable) The length of the Cone increases by 1 Space. Stagger: (1 SP) Each creature makes a Might Save. Save Failure: The target is unable to take Reactions for 1 Round.
entries.title: Scattershot

entries.keywords: Attack
entries.summary: 2 AP • Ranged Weapon
entries.text:
You bombard an area with a series of projectiles. Make an Area Martial Attack against the AD of every target within a 3 Space Diameter Sphere that’s Point of Origin is within Range. Hit: The target takes the damage of your Weapon. Close Quarters Penalty: You have DisADV on the Attack if you’re within the Melee Range of at least 1 enemy, unless that enemy is Incapacitated. DC Tip: Remember you have DisADV on any Attack beyond your Normal Range and you can’t attack beyond your Long Range.

Enhancements
Damage: (2 SP, Repeatable) The damage increases by 1. Area: (2 SP, Repeatable) The diameter of the Sphere increases by 1 Space. Rain of Fire: (1 SP) Targets within the area don’t gain the benefits of 1/2 Cover against this Attack. Suppressive Fire: (2 SP) Each creature makes a Charisma Save. Save Failure: The creature becomes Hindered for 1 Round
entries.title: Volley

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP • Self (or 1 Space if wielding a Melee Weapon or Shield)
entries.text:
You deflect an attack. Trigger: A target you can see within range (including yourself) is targeted by an Attack against its PD. Reaction: You grant the target a +5 bonus to its PD against this Attack.

Enhancements
Alert: (1 SP) The Attacker’s next Attack this turn against the target has DisADV. Disarm: (1 SP) If the Attacker is within 1 Space of you or the target, they make a Physical Save. Save Failure: The target drops the Weapon used for the Attack to the ground once the Attack is resolved. Save Failure (5): You gain possession of the Weapon, provided you have a free hand to hold it.
entries.title: Parry

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP • Self (or 1 Space if wielding a Shield)
entries.text:
You stand firm against an attack. Trigger: A target you can see within range (including yourself) is targeted by an Attack against its AD. Reaction: You grant the target a +5 bonus to its AD against this Attack.

Enhancements
Targets: (1 AP, Repeatable) You can target 1 additional creature within range that’s also targeted by the same Attack. Grapple: (1 SP) If the Attacker is within 1 Space of you, they make a Physical Save. Save Failure: The Attacker becomes Grappled by you once the Attack is resolved.
entries.title: Brace

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP • Self
entries.text:
You avoid an enemy attack by quick repositioning. Trigger: You’re targeted by an Attack. Reaction: You impose DisADV on the Attack against you. You can move 1 Space after the Attack, provided you stay within range of the Attack.

Enhancements
Evasion: (1 SP) You gain ADV on any Saves imposed by the Attack. Disengage: (1 SP) Movement made as part of this Maneuver doesn’t provoke Opportunity Attacks. Slip Away: (1 SP) You can move up to your Speed instead of 1 Space and you no longer need to stay in range of the Attack.
entries.title: Side Step

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP • 1 Space
entries.text:
You take damage for a nearby ally. Trigger: A target you can see within range is Hit by an Attack. Reaction: The damage of the Attack is shared between you and the target. The damage you take bypasses any Damage Reduction you have.

Enhancements
Targets: (1 AP, Repeatable) You can target 1 additional creature within range that’s also targeted by the same Attack. Taunt: (1 SP) The attacker makes a Charisma Save. Save Failure: They’re Taunted by you for 1 Round. Heroic Protect: (2 SP) The Attack made against your target is made against you instead. You take all of the damage and effects instead of them, and if the Attack is accompanied by a Save (as with a Dynamic Attack Save), you make the Save instead of the target. If you were also originally a target of the Attack, you resolve both separately. Resistance: (1 SP) You gain Resistance (Half) to any damage you take from using this Maneuver. The cost of this Enhancement increases by 1 SP if you use the Heroic Protect Enhancement.
entries.title: Protect

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Self (or 1 Space if wielding a Shield)
entries.text:
You push through an attack. Trigger: A target you can see within range (including yourself) is Hit by an Attack. Reaction: The target takes 1 less damage from the Attack.

Enhancements
Heroic Endure: (X SP) The target takes X less damage from the Attack. Steadfast: (1 SP) The target isn’t Vulnerable to damage from the Attack. Repel: (X SP) After the Attack, if the Attacker is within 1 Space of you or the target, they make a Might Save against your Save DC. Save Failure: They are pushed X Spaces away. Save Failure (each 5): +1 Space pushed.
entries.title: Endure

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Self
entries.text:
You take a moment to catch your breath and refocus. Make a DC 15 Martial Check. Failure: You gain 2 Temp HP for 1 Round. Success: You gain 3 Temp HP for 1 Round. Success (each 5): +1 Temp HP.

Enhancements
Increased Temp HP: (1 SP, Repeatable) You gain +2 Temp HP. Physical Resolve: (1 SP) You gain ADV on Physical Saves for the duration. Mental Resolve: (1 SP) You gain ADV on Mental Saves for the duration.
entries.title: Resolve

entries.keywords: Defense
entries.summary: 1 AP • 1 Space
entries.text:
You swap places with a nearby creature. You swap Spaces with a willing creature within range. If you or the target creature provoke Opportunity Attacks as a result of swapping Spaces, those Attacks are all made against you. Reaction: You can spend an additional 1 SP to perform this Maneuver as a Reaction in response to a creature within 1 Space being Attacked. When you do, you also impose DisADV on the Attack against them.

Enhancements
Escape: (1 SP) The target can immediately move up to its Speed after swapping Spaces. Seamless Swap:(1 SP) Swapping Spaces doesn’t provoke any Opportunity Attacks. Hostile Swap: (1 SP) You can target an unwilling creature. When you do, make a Martial Check against the target’s Physical Save. Check Success: You swap Spaces with them.
entries.title: Swap

entries.keywords: Grapple
entries.summary: 1 AP • Melee
entries.text:
You slam a Grappled creature. Make a Melee Martial Attack against the target’s AD. Hit: The target takes 1 Bludgeoning damage.

Enhancements
Finishing Slam: (1 SP) You deal 2 additional damage. The Grapple ends. Stunned: (2 SP, Repeatable) The target makes a Physical Save. Save Failure: They are Stunned 1 for 1 Round. You can use this Enhancement a maximum of two times. Wall Rake: (X SP) You slam 1 Grappled creature into a wall within 1 Space and move up to X Spaces along the wall, ending your movement within 1 Space of the wall. The target makes a Repeated Might Save against your Save DC. Save Failure: They gain Bleeding X per Space moved.
entries.title: Slam

entries.keywords: Grapple
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Melee
entries.text:
You restrain a grappled target. You make a Martial Check against the target’s Repeated Physical Save. Contest Success: The target is Restrained until the Grapple ends. DC Tip: A creature can spend 1 AP to attempt to break a Grapple (see “Grapple” on page 43 for more information).

Enhancements
Prone: (1 SP) The target also falls Prone (you don’t fall Prone unless you choose to do so). Chokehold: (2 SP) The target also can’t speak or breathe until they are no longer Restrained by you. DC Tip: A creature that can’t breathe begins holding their breath. In Combat, a creature’s Breath Duration is equal to its Might (minimum of 1) in Rounds.
entries.title: Restrain

entries.keywords: Grapple
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Melee
entries.text:
You reposition a grappled creature to shield yourself from damage. Trigger: A creature that’s not Grappled by you Hits you with an Attack. Reaction: Make a Martial Check against the Grappled target’s Might Save. Check Success: The damage from the Attack is shared by you and the Grappled creature, and you can move the Grappled creature to any Space adjacent to you immediately afterwards. DC Tip: If the triggering Attack involved a Save (as with a Dynamic Attack Save) that moves you or your Grapple target out of your reach, you can still perform this Maneuver to resolve the damage (as if it the Hit happens moments before the forced movement).

Enhancements
Switch: (1 SP) After you complete the Reaction, you switch places with the Grappled target. This movement doesn’t provoke Opportunity Attacks against either you or the target. Partial Block: (1 SP) Your portion of the shared damage is reduced to 0. Full Block: (2 SP) The Attack made against you is made against the Grappled creature instead. They take all of the damage and effects instead of you, and if the Attack is accompanied by a Save (as with a Dynamic Attack Save), they make the Save instead of the you. If they were also originally a target of the Attack, they resolve both separately.
entries.title: Body Block

entries.text:
When you throw a creature using the Throwing rules, you can add the following Maneuver Enhancements. When you do, you’re considered to be performing a Maneuver. See “Throwing” on page 161 for more information. DC Tip: Remember, throwing a creature ends the Grapple.

Enhancements
Increased Throw: (X SP) The target is thrown X Spaces further. Skyward: (2 SP) Your throw distance isn’t halved for vertical throws. Prone: (1 SP) The target also falls Prone.
entries.title: Throw Creature

entries.keywords: Utility
entries.summary: 1 AP • Self
entries.text:
You take a moment to catch your breath and refocus. You attempt to spend Rest Points to regain HP equal to the Rest Points spent. Make a DC 15 Martial Check. Failure: You can spend 2 Rest Points. Success: You can spend up to 3 Rest Points. Success (each 5): You can spend 1 additional Rest Point.

Enhancements
Increased Healing: (1 AP or 1 SP, Repeatable) You can spend 1 additional Rest Point. Repeat Save: (1 AP or 1 SP) You can repeat a Save against an effect you’re subjected to.
entries.title: Recover

entries.keywords: Utility
entries.text:
When you take the Pass Through Action, you can add the following Maneuver Enhancements. When you add a Maneuver Enhancement (or perform the Action using SP), you’re considered to be performing a Maneuver. Stamina Action: You can spend SP instead of AP to perform the Pass Through Action.

Enhancements
Brush Past: (1 SP) The creature’s Space isn’t considered Difficult Terrain for this movement and you don’t provoke an Opportunity Attack from them if you leave their reach as part of the same movement. Let’s Go: (1 SP) On a Success, you can pull a willing creature within 1 Space of you to an unoccupied Space within 1 Space of the creature you pass.
entries.title: Heroic Pass Through

entries.keywords: Utility
entries.summary: 2 AP + 1 SP • Self
entries.text:
You run through a line of enemies. You move in a Line up to your Speed and make a Martial Check. Each creature within the Line must make a Physical Save against your Martial Check when you attempt to move through its Space. Contest Failure: You’re unable to move through the creature’s Space, preventing you from moving any further. Contest Success: You can move through the creature’s Space and they are knocked Prone. Example: You make a Martial Check with a result of 15. If your Speed is 5, you can move up to 5 Spaces in a straight Line. If there are 3 creatures in that Line, your Martial Check of 15 would be compared to a Martial Check each creature makes as you attempt to pass through their Space, one by one. If the first creature in your path gets a 15 or higher, you can’t pass through their Space and stop moving.

Enhancements
Distance: (1 SP, Repeatable) You can move up to an additional half your Speed. Brush Past: (1 SP) The Space of every creature who fails the contest isn’t considered Difficult Terrain for this movement and you don’t provoke an Opportunity Attack from them.
entries.title: Line Run

entries.keywords: Utility
entries.summary: 1 AP + 1 SP • Self
entries.text:
Sprint across the battlefield

Trigger: A creature ends their turn. Reaction: You immediately move up to your Speed.

Enhancements
Agile: (1 SP) You ignore Difficult Terrain during this movement. Disengage: (1 AP) You gain the benefits of the Disengage Action for the Movement. When you use this Enhancement, you can spend 1 additional SP to gain the benefits of the Full Disengage Action instead. Coordinated Movement: (2 SP, Repeatable) A willing creature of your choice within 1 Space of your original position can move without spending its own movement, provided they’re able to move and they end their movement within 1 Space of your destination.
entries.title: Reposition

Enhancements

Legendary Taunt: (1 SP) Creatures other than you have Resistance (Half) to damage dealt by the Taunted targets, provided the target isn’t also Taunted by those creatures. Mass Taunt: (1 AP + 1 SP) You instead target each creature of your choice within 5 Spaces that can see or hear you. When you choose this Enhancement, the cost of all other Enhancements (except Sustained) is doubled.

Frightened: (1 SP) Targets are Frightened instead. Mass Intimidate: (1 AP + 1 SP) You instead target each creature of your choice within 5 Spaces that can see or hear you. When you choose this Enhancement, the cost of all other Enhancements (except Sustained) is doubled.

Mass Shove: (1 AP + 1 SP) You instead target each creature of your choice within a 1 Space Aura. When you choose this Enhancement, the cost of all other Enhancements (except Stand Up) is doubled.

When you add a Maneuver Enhancement (or perform the Action using SP), you’re considered to be performing a Maneuver. Stamina Action: You can spend SP instead of AP to perform the Extend Jump Action.

Enhancements
Instant Jump: (1 SP) If performing a Standing Jump, your Jump Distances isn’t halved. Increased Jump: (1 SP, Repeatable) Your Jump Distance is increased by 2 for the Jump. Heroic Landing: (1 SP, Repeatable) You reduce any damage from falling by 2 for the Jump.

entries.keywords: Arcane Astromancy Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing 1 AP 10 Spaces
entries.summary: Arcane • Astromancy • 1 AP • 10 Spaces • Instantaneous
entries.text:
Tags: Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing

You conjure a bolt of pure magical energy that homes in on a target. Make a Ranged Spell Attack against the AD of a target within range. Hit: The target takes 1 Bludgeoning, Slashing or Piercing damage (your choice).

Enhancements
Range: (1 AP, Repeatable) The range of the Spell increases by 5 Spaces. You can use this Enhancement a maximum of two times. Damage: (X AP, Repeatable) The damage increases by X against 1 target of your choice. Arcane Missiles: (1 AP + X MP) Choose X additional targets within range using the same Spell Attack for all targets. The AP cost of this Enhancement can’t be paid for with MP. Autonomous: (1 MP) You can Attack a target you’ve seen since the start of your last turn, provided it’s within range and there’s a path between you and the target the projectile can follow. This attack ignores 1/2 or 3/4 Cover and you don’t have DisADV if the target is Unseen by you.

entries.summary: Arcane • Astromancy • 2 AP • Self • Instantaneous
entries.text:
Tags: Bludgeoning, Deafened, Motion, Piercing, Slashing

You produce a burst of destructive energy that envelops a 3 Space Cone. Make an Area Spell Attack against the AD of every target within the area. Hit: The target takes 1 Bludgeoning, Slashing or Piercing damage (your choice).

Enhancements
Damage: (X MP) The damage increases by X. Area: (X MP) The length of the Cone increases by X Spaces. Fractured: (1 MP) The Area becomes Difficult Terrain. A creature can spend 1 AP to clear 1 Space of this Difficult Terrain returning the Space to normal. Reverberate: (X MP) Each target makes a Physical Save. Save Failure: The target is pulled toward you or pushed away from you up to X Spaces (your choice) and is Deafened for 1 Round.
entries.title: Arcane Wave

entries.keywords: Arcane, Divine Astromancy Incapacitated, Planes, Psychic, Teleportation 1 AP + 2 MP 10 Spaces
entries.summary: Arcane, Divine • Astromancy • 1 AP + 2 MP • 10 Spaces • 1 Minute (Sustained)
entries.text:
Tags: Incapacitated, Planes, Psychic, Teleportation

You attempt to sever a target’s link to this plane. Make a Spell Check against the Repeated Charisma Save of a target within range. Check Success: The target is banished to a harmless demiplane for the duration. If the target is native to another plane, it is sent back to its home plane instead. While banished, the target is Incapacitated and cannot affect or be affected by anything on the plane it is banished from. When the Spell ends, the creature reappears in the Space it left, or the nearest unoccupied Space. If it was banished to its home plane for 1 minute, the effect becomes permanent (GMs discretion).

Enhancements
Range: (1 AP, Repeatable) The range of the Spell increases by 5 Spaces. You can use this Enhancement a maximum of two times. Severing Seal: (1 MP) If the effect of the Spell becomes permanent, you can create a temporary seal preventing the creature from returning. The creature can’t return to the plane it was banished from for 24 hours. Planar Tear: (X MP) You cause a tear in the fabric of the planes to appear in a 3 Space diameter Sphere centered on the Spaces the creature occupied. When a creature enters the area for the first time on its turn, or starts its turn there, it makes a Charisma Save against your Save DC. Save Failure: The target takes X Psychic damage. The tear disappears when the Spell ends.
entries.title: Banish

entries.keywords: Arcane, Primal Astromancy Air, Embolden, Gravity, Motion 1 AP + 1 MP 10 Spaces
entries.summary: Arcane, Primal • Astromancy • 1 AP + 1 MP • 10 Spaces • 10 Minutes (Sustained)
entries.text:
Tags: Air, Embolden, Gravity, Motion

You grant a creature with range the following benefits for the duration:
• Glide Speed: They can use their movement to glide horizontally in the air.
• Altitude Drop: If they end their turn midair, they Control Fall 4 Spaces.
• Controlled Falling: They suffer no damage from Controlled Falling. Spell Cast: When you cast the Spell, make a DC 15 Spell Check. Success: The target can immediately move in any direction (including vertically) up to their Speed.

Enhancements
Range: (1 AP, Repeatable) The range of the Spell increases by 5 Spaces. You can use this Enhancement a maximum of two times. Duration: (1 MP, Repeatable) The duration increases by 1 step (10 minutes -> 1 hour -> 8 hours -> Long Rest). Targets: (1 AP + X MP) You can target X additional creatures within range. The AP cost of this Enhancement can’t be paid for with MP. Hover: (1 MP) The target isn’t effected by Altitude Drop and instead hovers in place when not moving, even while Unconscious or Prone. Fly: (2 MP) The target isn’t effected by Altitude Drop and gains a Fly Speed equal to its Speed for the duration.
entries.title: Blessing of Air
